target.statement: DK-GBMKKM achieves ACC = 0.6717 (average over 12 datasets) — or, cheapest single cell, its ACC on the smallest dataset (lung discrete, n=73) as shown in Fig. 2 / Appendix G
target.table_ref: Table I (average ACC row for DK-GBMKKM); per-dataset ACC in Fig. 2
target.dataset: lung discrete (73 samples, 325 features, 7 classes) — smallest of the 12 public datasets

compute.basis: Paper is MATLAB-only (R2025b) with no stated Python port; an agent must reimplement GBCT ball generation in kernel space, the ball-level MKKM alternating optimization, and the 12-kernel construction, then run on a 73-sample dataset — cheap numerically but expensive in reimplementation/debugging and MATLAB-licence avoidance.

blockers: Reference implementation is MATLAB (R2025b), not Python; agent must reimplement the full GBCT + dynamic ball-update pipeline from the appendix
GBCT (ref [22]) splitting procedure is only cited, not fully specified in this paper
Headline Table I number requires all 12 datasets and 8 methods (7 baselines), far beyond one cell
Baseline implementations (SMKC, AASC, MKKM-SR, GB-MKKM) are separate MATLAB codebases
title: DK-GBMKKM: Dynamic Kernel-Space Granular-Ball Multiple Kernel $k$-Means Clustering
